glm.feedback:
## Findings - Category: test Severity: medium File: `integration-tests/test_e2e_real_fixture.py` (~line at `if "Reply draft" in text:`) Finding: The mockup-draft check is conditional on the literal string `Reply draft` appearing in the mockup HTML. If mockup 03's card heading or markup changes (or the draft card is dropped), the assertion is silently skipped and the test still passes — exactly the drift AC3 is meant to catch. There is no assertion that the draft branch executed at least once. Suggestion: Track whether any draft was checked (`drafts_checked += 1`) and assert `drafts_checked >= 1` (or assert `"Reply draft" in text` for `03-reply-draft` specifically) so the template-vs-mockup guarantee cannot be vacuously satisfied. - Category: test Severity: medium File: `integration-tests/test_e2e_real_fixture.py` (list-row loop at the end of `test_mockup_text_equals_...`) Finding: The list-row check iterates `re.findall(r'u/(.*?)
(.*?)
', ...)`; if the row markup changes so the regex matches zero rows, the loop body never runs and the test passes vacuously. `checked == 3` also only counts loop iterations for the three screens, not that content was verified. Suggestion: Assert a positive row count (e.g. `rows > 0` per mockup, and that the five expected Reddit titles each appear as rows somewhere), so a markup change fails loudly instead of passing. - Category: test Severity: low File: `integration-tests/test_e2e_real_fixture.py` (`test_shipped_recordings_...`) Finding: The Python test asserts only `>= 2` items older than 14 days, while the expected-result file and the new `real-variant.spec.ts` test pin `old: 3` exactly. A future edit that drops one old item would pass the Python test and fail the TS test — inconsistent pins. (AC1 only requires >=2, so this is a consistency issue, not an AC violation.) Suggestion: Align the Python assertion to `== 3` to match the other pins, or leave a comment explaining why it's deliberately looser. - Category: spec Severity: low File: `integration-tests/fixtures/social-engagement-real/brief.json` (`package_sha256`) Finding: The spec says the recordings are "copied unchanged from run 14" and AC4 requires the new hash / warning-free package; neither the provenance nor that `package_sha256` matches the new tree can be verified from the diff alone. If the hash was not regenerated after adding the files, package-hash checks elsewhere will fail. Suggestion: Confirm the hash was computed over the final tree (including the two new JSON files and updated brief.md/expected-result) — e.g. by running the existing package-hash test. Non-issues I checked: the shipped data satisfies 12 items, 4/4/4, three items >14 days older than the newest (10-28 vs 10-04, 09-30, 10-02), 12 distinct URLs, all `.example` hosts; the `_summarize`/`_shorten` helpers match the brief's regex, collapse, and 300/400-char cut rules; the named-thread fit criteria in brief.md are consistent with the shipped data (quiet_lantern_42 / copper_fieldmouse); mockups are untouched as required; no security concerns (invented hosts/authors, no secrets, test-only code). Overall: the change implements the spec and the acceptance criteria; the findings are test-hardening refinements, chiefly that the draft and list-row mockup checks can pass vacuously. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
